items.title: skynox7: Proxyjacking Edge Devices Into Residential Proxies
items.summary: Adversaries have a wide range of mechanisms they can use to obfuscate their public internet protocol (IP) addresses to avoid attribution and reduce their detectable signature. Adversaries have used various types of nodes and services to proxy their traffic including commercial virtual private networks (VPN), virtual private servers (VPS), co-opted victim infrastructure, and more. Over time, defenders have been able to use adversary choices in infrastructure to surface illegitimate activity. For example, “It’s not normal for our users to login from IP addresses associated with this or any VPS provider.” Some stealthy adversaries are using residential proxies, which fundamentally break some of the core assumptions about the detectable characteristics of infrastructure used for malicious activity. GreyNoise helped an organization identify one of these stealthy intrusions and separately revealed a malicious cyber actor conducting a proxyjacking campaign.

items.title: TAG-217 Targets South Korean Financial Services with ARTEX
items.summary: The threat actor linked to recent AI-assisted attacks on South Korean financial institutions was testing infrastructure and assembling attack tools as early as August 2026, weeks before the banking campaign became public, according to new research from Recorded Future’s Insikt Group. Subsequent public reporting indicated that the breaches exposed personal data belonging to at least 68,000 people across at least seven financial institutions. Insikt Group’s investigation expands the known timeline and capabilities of the actor, tracked as TAG-217. Insikt Group uncovered tools designed to steal cryptocurrency wallet files, gain greater access to Linux systems, and test weaknesses in mobile devices. The findings illustrate the “jagged edge” of AI-enabled attacks: threat actors realizing significant gains while committing basic operational security mistakes. AI helps attackers pursue more targets across more environments, but does not prevent them from making the security mistakes that allowed Recorded Future to uncover preparations and capabilities beyond the reported banking campaign. Those mistakes give defenders opportunities to identify related activity and disrupt operations.

items.title: Moxa Vulnerabilities in Industrial Computing Products
items.summary: Classification: Severe, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv3.1: 8.6, CVEs: CVE-2026-109812, CVE-2026-109813, Summary: This security advisory addresses two vulnerabilities identified in industrial computing products. CVE-2026-109812 - Missing Authorization on Secret Endpoints A missing authorization vulnerability exists in the internal API `/api/v1/secrets/` of some of Moxa's industrial computing products. A low-privileged authenticated attacker with adjacent network access could exploit this vulnerability to access sensitive information, potentially resulting in the disclosure of confidential data, including cryptographic key material. CVE-2026-109813 - Shared Hard-coded Root CA Private Key A hard-coded cryptographic key vulnerability exists in the `/usr/bin/sysman` of some of Moxa's industrial computing products. An unauthenticated attacker with adjacent network access could exploit the exposed private key material to compromise the confidentiality and integrity of communications.

items.title: Investigating Ephemeral Supply Chain Tampering
items.summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) and Mandiant investigated a software supply chain compromise campaign targeting the update infrastructure belonging to AOMEI Technology between April 2026 and July 2026. The threat actor conducted repeated, short-burst configuration tampering against AOMEI origin servers. Each tampering window remained active for only five to ten minutes before reverting to authentic versions. This is the first time that we have encountered a software supply chain compromise that was implemented with these very short windows, effectively evading traditional point-in-time triage and automated file scanning. The campaign delivered a multi-stage payload chain involving the newly tracked CROSSROAD downloader and SHINYROAD backdoor. The threat actor iteratively modified its tradecraft, pivoting its staging infrastructure from cloud providers to dedicated domains and legitimate cloud storage. This evolving staging setup makes it particularly challenging for defenders to establish effective infrastructure-based blocking or network controls. We attribute this activity to a threat cluster we are tracking as UNC7017.

items.title: AI-Powered Espionage Campaign Targets Government Linux Infrastructure
items.summary: Unit 42 identified a campaign targeting government entities and state-affiliated infrastructure, with observed activity spanning from October 2025–April 2026. We track this activity as CL-UNK-1211. In the operations we witnessed, the attackers relied on AI-generated payloads. Multiple artifacts deployed throughout the intrusion contained AI-made conversational annotations and developer reasoning comments, suggesting that the code was either generated using large language models (LLMs) or executed by an automated AI agent. The attackers behind this cluster of activity focused on Linux environments to conduct extensive reconnaissance and maintain persistent network access to support intelligence-gathering. The attackers attempted to dump sensitive databases and exfiltrate government mailboxes to access social media accounts. The campaign included a diverse toolkit that combined open-source tools, custom cross-platform backdoors and widespread web shell deployments. We observed various defense evasion techniques, including attempts to disable endpoint protections, erase system logs and plant deceptive red-team markers to disguise activity as a legitimate security assessment. Our attribution of this activity to CL-UNK-1211 is in accordance with the Unit 42 attribution framework. We designate the term UNK to clusters of activity whose affiliation with either nation-state or cybercrime activity we have not yet determined.

items.title: BAE Systems cyberattack disrupts US federal court operations
items.summary: The Administrative Office of the US Courts (AOUSC) says a cyberattack on government contractor BAE Systems has taken down the notice system used by federal bankruptcy courts. In a Thursday press release, the Administrative Office of the US Courts said the BAE Systems cyberattack also halted the production and distribution of bankruptcy notices. "The Administrative Office of the US Courts has been in communication with the impacted courts and is also coordinating with BAE Systems. BAE is actively investigating this incident and working to restore operations," AOUSC said. "As a result of the incident, all access to the BNC systems and websites that BAE operates on behalf of the Judiciary and the related bankruptcy noticing process are unavailable at this time, including bnc.uscourts.gov, bankruptcynotices.uscourts.gov, notices.uscourts.gov, and the National Creditor Registration Service."

items.title: F-Secure Launches Victim-First Scam Encyclopedia Covering 50+ Types of Consumer Fraud
items.summary: There are more than 50 distinct ways to scam someone online, and F-Secure's Threat Intelligence team catalogued them all in its new Scam Encyclopedia,one of the most comprehensive guides to scams and fraudavailable today. Built from decades of research, the continuously updated, living guide covers both established scams and new methods most people haven't heard of yet. Unlike similar resources available online, the Scam Encyclopedia emphasizes a different point of view: every scam is explained from the victim's perspective, covering what they see, what they're told, what they're asked to do, and where exactly the "scam" comes in. That structure makes it easier for readers to recognize the same pattern in their own lives, before they become a victim themselves.

items.title: Exposing AdFection: How Discover-Tech Turned Targeted Ads Into a Pipeline for Zero-Click Mercenary Spyware
items.summary: This is the first-ever public confirmation of zero-click mercenary spyware delivered via targeted ads. We call the technique AdFection, and show how it was used to infect devices at Al Jazeera with Candiru’s spyware. We also uncover Discover-Tech, and show how the company helps mercenary surveillance vendors track and hack devices around the world. Devices at international news network Al Jazeera were infected with mercenary spyware from Candiru (rebranded as “Integrity Labs”) via targeted online advertisements. We provide the first public technical confirmation of a zero-click mercenary spyware attack delivered via targeted advertising, which we call AdFection. The malicious advertisements were purchased by Discover-Tech, an Israeli company that presents itself as a legitimate advertising company, but which we found operates as a facilitator for multiple mercenary spyware partners. Discover-Tech operates a platform called Controlium that enables its mercenary partners to de-anonymize, fingerprint, and automatically infect devices the moment an advertisement is rendered — a form of zero-click attack. Analysis of four billion Discover-Tech bidding records shows that during a four-month period, the company’s ads were shown on almost 200,000 unique websites and Android/iOS apps in dozens of countries.

items.title: BeyondTrust patches zero-day exploited in attacks since August
items.summary: BeyondTrust warned customers on Thursday to patch a critical flaw in its Remote Support (RS) that has been exploited in zero-day attacks since late August. Remote Support is the company's enterprise-grade support solution that helps IT service desks, help desks, and customer support teams troubleshoot issues remotely. Tracked as CVE-2026-102764, this actively exploited authentication bypass vulnerability lets unprivileged remote attackers perform file operations on unpatched appliances and affects RS 26.2.3 or earlier. BeyondTrust patched the security issue for all Remote Support and Privileged Remote Access SaaS customers on October 8, but self-hosted installations must be patched manually if automatic updates are not enabled. "While our internal testing has not identified any way for an attacker to exploit this vulnerability in Privileged Remote Access, PRA shares the affected code, so out of an abundance of caution, we have released the patch for PRA and recommend self-hosted Privileged Remote Access customers apply it immediately," BeyondTrust said.

items.title: ARMORY CASTLE Exploits BeyondTrust
items.summary: On October 15, BeyondTrust disclosed a vulnerability, CVE-2026-102764, impacting BeyondTrust Remote Support (formerly Bomgar) appliances. BeyondTrust Remote Support is an enterprise secure remote access solution that enables IT teams to securely access and troubleshoot remote endpoints. The successful exploitation of this vulnerability results in the arbitrary upload of files. During an incident response engagement, Mandiant identified evidence that ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus espionage threat actor (formerly tracked as UNC5221), exploited this vulnerability as a zero-day, in late August 2026. This blog describes how ARMORY CASTLE escalated privileges and established persistent access to compromised BeyondTrust Remote Support appliances following exploitation of CVE-2026-102764, and provides actionable guidance for defenders. Organizations should prepare for potential widespread exploitation following this disclosure, as ARMORY CASTLE and other threat actors have historically conducted broad, opportunistic exploitation once the vulnerability becomes public.
